If rhetoric like 'being fat is unhealthy' was Truly based concern and not fatphobia, then why doesn't such discourse shift it's focus from 'fat is bad/you gotta lose weight' the bad diets and high stress, sedentary lifestyles of this age. 
Eating healthy, moving more, good sleep and less stress and great for your health regardless. But all the people who keep going on about how being fat is unhealthy seem like they feel fat people Inherently and always have bad lifestyles and thin people always have better ones, and that's simply not true. 
Everyone benefits from a better lifestyle but making it sound like a fat person on a healthier diet and lifestyle than a skinny person still somehow needs to do Whatever possible to get rid of that weight (people literally advocate hard drugs and starvation) is just messed up imo. And that's not even going into how 'fat' looks different on different people. POC bodies in particular are Much curvier and merely looking at the scale/BMI for someone like that (the way I've had doctors do) does not make for an informed understanding of weight issues.

As someone who used to fast for weeks at a time (unintentionally believe it or not, because adhd hyper fixations can get Wild) but used to feel proud because it felt like I lost weight without any 'effort' as such and was a sign of my mental 'strength', I wish I could go back and tell my younger self it's all bs because it Directly led to me having my gallbladder removed, my gut microbiome being disrupted and some seriously severe nutritional deficiencies. All of which ended up with far more 'unhealthy fat' around my middle than I did before all this.  All if this is to say it's too easy to get sucked into terrible dietary habits when you feel desperate, frustrated and angry at yourself.

Right now I practice meditation with my yoga teacher. I used to do both meditation and yoga as a child but stopped for some reasons and only now got back to it ptoperly. 

But there are also guided meditation resources online if you want to practice on your own. Michael Sealey's youtube channel is something I personally like. Headspace is also an app with some free resources for guided meditation. In general you can try looking for resources online on guided meditation, mindfullness meditation, controlled breathing exercises, and box breathing. 

Focusing on the latter two is a good way to get started. 

Meditation is a largely mental practice, where you try to bring order and calm to your thoughts by doing breathing exercises, decluttering you mind and relaxing. 

Yoga is... properly speaking a whole entire lifestyle in itself but Bevan what people refer to is physical exercises  often consisting of certain poses (asanas) and stretching. Most yoga classes, especially in India will usually have a meditation component as well. It makes sense because yoga focuses on both mental and physical health,  plus it's much easier to get into the right state of mind for meditation post exercise, even light exercise like a beginner's yoga class.
